name: Renfield Shake Motor
description:
12V shake motor - 'the signature', Renfield's tremble. BTS7960 / IBT-2 module (sold as HW-039), 43A dual half-bridge. BCM GPIO: RPWM=12, LPWM=13 (header pins 32 and 33).

PIN CHOICE: both RPWM and LPWM carry PWM on this board (one at a time, by direction) - unlike the MDD10A where DIR was a static level. lgpio.tx_pwm() is SOFTWARE PWM and runs on any GPIO, so nothing today depends on this, but 12 and 13 are the Pi 5's RP1 hardware-PWM pair (dtoverlay=pwm-pi5) and are therefore the only pins that would not need rewiring if hardware PWM is ever added. Neither collides with I2C, SPI or UART, and nothing else on Renfield uses them.

ENABLES ARE JUMPERED HIGH IN HARDWARE, not driven from GPIO. linear_actuator_control_v2.py claims renPin/lenPin, writes them HIGH once at setup and never touches them again (setup_bts7960_pins), so a GPIO adds nothing a jumper to VCC does not. Tying R_EN and L_EN to VCC on the board saves two GPIOs and removes the GPIO_BUSY (-79) trap that a shared enable pin used to cause. Do NOT re-add renPin/lenPin unless you actually need a software disable, and if you do, give each its own line.

VCC IS A SEPARATE 5V SUPPLY. Unlike the MDD10A this board does NOT power its logic from the motor rail: VCC goes to a Pi 5V pin (header 2 or 4) and GND to a Pi ground pin. With VCC unconnected nothing moves and every command still returns success - it fails exactly like a wiring mystery. Never put 12V on VCC; it destroys the board. Inputs are 3.3V-compatible, so RPWM/LPWM go straight to the Pi with no level shifter. R_IS/L_IS stay unconnected.

WIRING: B+/B- to the 12V supply, M+/M- to the motor, nothing else in the 12V path but a slow-blow fuse. No bulk capacitor, no snubber, no series resistor. A fixed resistor can NEVER sit in line with the motor supply - 200 ohm allows 60mA and pins the board near 3.3V; a pre-charge resistor is only valid across a switch that shorts it out.

HISTORY: a Cytron MDD10A was wired here on 2026-09-13 and failed with smoke after a couple of minutes powered. Root cause not conclusively established - a reverse-connected bulk electrolytic is the leading candidate (that timescale is its signature) and a bare capacitor used as a snubber is second. The Pi survived. Prove this board with a jumper wire before involving the Pi: 12V on B+/B-, 5V on VCC, enables high, then touch RPWM to 5V - the motor should turn.

Shake is a short burst: scenes run 900-2000ms at 50-80% and maxDuration caps any single energization at 5000ms. A wiper-class motor stalls around 24-40A; a stalled motor cooks until the fuse opens and PWM outlives the process (Groundbreaker, 2026-08-30).
